# file: # THE HOST JUDGE'S TEST PLANS, DEDUPLICATED (2026-11-11; docs/rust-port/PHASE3_SHIM_DESIGN.md section 10 ruling 18;
# docs/rust-port/PHASE3.md step 0): every test plan a host-judge row names, once, 16,247 plans of 30,212,521,643
# characters, rebuilt exactly from four files. THE FORMAT is rust/tools/test-plan-texts.py's header (the writer, the
# reader and the check: a tool, not a probe, since reading this oracle needs it). In short: a JSON value of a plan (a
# string, an array or an object) of at least 8,192 bytes that occurs twice or more in the archive, nested ones too, is
# stored once in the values store under its key (the SHA-256 of its text's UTF-16 units, little-endian: a plan's id
# rule), and its place in a plan's text, or in a bigger value's, holds a reference: U+0001, the key's 64 hex digits,
# U+0001. Java's compact JSON writer never writes a character below U+0020 (Json.escapeTo escapes every one inside a
# string; outside strings it writes none), and the archive holds none, so a reference is never Java's text. Rebuilding
# splits a text on U+0001 and puts each value back, rebuilt the same way. Each store is independent zstd frames of up to
# 2 MiB (`zstd -19`, zstd 1.5.7; plain `zstd -d` reads a store whole), so one plan reads its plans frame and its values'
# frames only: 65 to 83 ms a plan from a fresh reader (two runs), decompressing a median 5.6 MB of the 246 MB; 10 to 12
# ms a plan from one reader. WHAT REPEATS (measured first): one 516,123-byte CSV (testDataSetupCsv, the stress suites'
# seed data) stands 31,494 times in 10,498 plans (16.3 GB), and SQL strings 4.5 GB more; but whole JSON strings
# deduplicated still leave 4.9 GB of plan text even from 64 bytes, since whole sub-objects repeat across a suite's plans
# (the session, the seed steps, MIR trees); whole values leave 154 MB of plan text and 26,551 values (91 MB). The four
# MADE by `python3 rust/tools/test-plan-texts.py write <the archive below> <dir>` (its defaults, --min 8192 --frame
# 2097152), twice, byte for byte the same. CHECKED 2026-11-11 by `check rust/oracles/plan --sha <the archive's SHA-256>
# --ids rust/oracles/plan/plan-ids.tsv.zst`: all 16,247 plans rebuilt, each hashing to its id; every value's rebuilt text
# to its key; every frame its row of the frame table; the index every value's frame; the rebuilt archive's SHA-256 the
# archive's (below); the plans' ids exactly the test plan ids the host judge's rows name in plan-ids.
